questions.stem: Five friends — A, B, C, D, E — like five different colours: red, blue, green, yellow, white. A likes blue. D likes white. E likes yellow. B does not like red. C likes:
questions.explanation: A = Blue, D = White, E = Yellow. Remaining colours {Red, Green} for B and C. B does not like red, so B = Green. C must take the remaining colour = Red. Distractor 1 already taken by A. Distractor 3 belongs to B (because B avoids red). Distractor 4 already taken by D.

questions.stem: Four students — P, Q, R, S — sat for different subjects (Math, Physics, Chemistry, Biology). P did NOT sit for Physics or Biology. R sat for Chemistry. S sat for Physics. Q sat for which subject?
questions.explanation: R = Chemistry; S = Physics. P avoids Physics and Biology → P ∈ {Math, Chemistry}; Chemistry is taken, so P = Math. Q gets the remaining subject = Biology. Distractor 1 belongs to P. Distractor 3 belongs to S. Distractor 4 belongs to R.

questions.stem: Three boys — Akash, Bobby, Chandu — are of three different ages: 12, 15, 18. Akash is the oldest. Chandu is younger than Bobby. Bobby's age is:
questions.explanation: Akash is oldest → Akash = 18. Chandu < Bobby → Bobby is the older of the remaining two. Remaining ages {12, 15} → Bobby = 15, Chandu = 12. Distractor 12 swaps Bobby and Chandu. Distractor 18 ignores Akash being oldest. 'Cannot be determined' is wrong because the constraints fully fix the order.

questions.stem: Six people P, Q, R, S, T, U sit in a row facing north. P is at the extreme left. Q is immediately right of P. R is immediately right of Q. T is immediately right of R. S is at the extreme right. The position of T (counting from left) is:
questions.explanation: P = 1, Q = 2, R = 3, T = 4. S = 6 (extreme right). U gets the only remaining slot = 5. So T is at position 4 from the left. Distractor 1 confuses T with R. Distractor 3 confuses T with U. Distractor 4 confuses T with Q.

questions.stem: Five cities — A, B, C, D, E — have populations 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 crore (one each). A has the largest. B has 4 crore. E has 1 crore. C has fewer people than D. C's population (in crore) is:
questions.explanation: A = 5 (largest); B = 4; E = 1. Remaining values {2, 3} for C and D. C < D forces C = 2, D = 3. Distractor 1 confuses C with E. Distractor 3 swaps C and D. Distractor 5 confuses C with A.

questions.stem: Four cars are parked in a row. The red car is to the left of the blue car. The black car is to the left of the red car. The white car is to the right of the blue car. The order from left to right is:
questions.explanation: Constraints: Black < Red, Red < Blue, Blue < White (using '<' for 'to-the-left-of'). Chain: Black < Red < Blue < White. So order: Black, Red, Blue, White. Distractor 1 reverses Black and Red. Distractor 3 swaps Red and Blue. Distractor 4 reverses the whole order.

questions.stem: Four books — A, B, C, D — are stacked vertically. A is above B. D is between A and B. C is below B. The bottom-most book is:
questions.explanation: A above B + D between A and B → top-to-bottom order: A, D, B. C is below B → C is the bottom-most. Final stack top→bottom: A, D, B, C. Distractor 1 confuses A (top-most) with the bottom. Distractor 3 places B at bottom, ignoring the 'C below B' clue. Distractor 4 confuses D (middle) with the bottom.
